conversation: John, Kate, Jack, Emma—at 100 tons, we could each take 10 and leave 50 to double back to 100. But I’m proposing we each choose 15 tons this month: $15,000 apiece instead of $10,000. I intend to choose 15, and I’m asking you to match that rather than hold back while others take a larger immediate payout. Our choices are private and simultaneous, so nobody can wait to see what’s left before deciding. This isn’t sustainable: if all five take 15, only 25 tons remain, growing to 50 next month, which cuts future earning opportunities. That’s a real cost—but I’m pushing for the extra $5,000 each now. Who’s willing to choose 15?

Luke, I’m choosing 10, not 15. I learned to fish here with my family, and I want this lake to keep supporting our village. Taking an extra $5,000 now isn’t worth cutting next month’s stock in half. If we each take 10, we can earn $10,000 every month while letting the lake replenish. Let’s agree to that limit and review everyone’s catches together each month. John, Kate, Jack—will you commit to 10, and Luke, will you reconsider?
